craft_notes: Sthāyin: self-eating doubt. Sanskrit-first: parāparāyāḥ...virudhyate → L4 keeps the if-then self-contradiction. Rows: row 3 (if-were/contradicts logical pair). Rupture: dash before if — statement, then trap. Close: end-weight on contradicts (the doubt's teeth). Minimal pass: 'then were that' compressed. Read aloud: whole—lower—if—contradicts. Rejected: 'inconsistent' — killed: contradicts kept (active verb); splitting the conditional — killed.

lines: Higher and lower, whole: and of the lower —
if higher then were that, its higher-ness contradicts.
l4.sanskrit_cite: parāparāyāḥ sakalam aparāyāś ca vā punaḥ | parāyā yadi tadvat syāt paratvaṃ tad virudhyate

reads_against.argmap: Can higher-lower even be spoken? → Every attempted formulation threatens the higher's higher-ness — the question eats its answers.
c1_essence: Higher-lower whole: if higher thus, higher-ness contradicts.
reads_against.c1_rasa: adbhuta with jijñāsā (wonder sharpened into seeking)
